html:
A gold covered Buddhist stupa in Vientiane, the capital of Laos, built in its present form in 1566. It is the national symbol of Laos and appears on its national emblem.

Legends say a stupa holding a relic of the Buddha stood here as early as the 3rd century, and the site may have held an older Khmer temple. The great stupa was built by King Setthathirath of Lan Xang, who had moved his capital from Luang Prabang to Vientiane in 1560, partly to stay further from the armies of Burma. It rises in tiers from a square base to a tall, slim spire.

In 1828 Siamese armies sacked Vientiane after the revolt of the Lao king Anouvong, and the stupa was badly damaged. French scholars and the colonial government of French Indochina restored it, and after a first attempt was judged wrong, rebuilt it in the 1930s. Each November a festival brings monks and pilgrims from across Laos.
